claim: subject advances through discrete flip-book frames/poses on scroll

q1_defects.answer: No defects. Card is sharp at every pose; chrome (brass header, ice dot, 3 grey rows, rounded panel) intact through every rotation. bandingScore drops to ~0.25 during play (clean).

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads as a flip-book: idle=flat front card, play-1=card rotated diagonally ~30 deg, play-3=card flipped 90 deg to portrait (brass header now a vertical bar, dot moved to bottom-right). Discrete advancing poses, full card preserved at each, matches the ground-truth card.

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. frames control changes pose granularity (low snaps to a flat near-vertical pose, high lands on a smoother intermediate angle); holdRatio changes which held pose appears at the pinned scroll point; jitter adds a small rotation offset. All three produce visibly distinct poses.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive: pose advances across play frames, frameDeltaMag ~10-11.6; controls apply ~571-585ms, all changed:true.

q5_net.answer: PLEASED — it genuinely looks like a card being flipped through discrete frames, the card look never breaks, and the knobs change the pose sensibly.

flags.note: jitter control is the subtlest of the three (changedFrac 0.0816); a first-time user might not immediately notice it, though the pose angle does differ between low and high.
